ground_truth.title: Here Are the 8 Best Employee Management Software for HR Teams
ground_truth.author: Dakota Hebert
ground_truth.main_content:
Quick Summary 

We tested 8 employee management platforms on features, pricing, and ease of use. Checkwriters stands out for its all-in-one approach and dedicated support, while ADP is great for large enterprises and Connecteam works well for mobile teams. Use our comparison table to find your fit.

Seamless Employee Management Starts With the Right Software

Managing employees is more complex than ever. HR professionals juggle onboarding, time tracking, benefits administration, and performance reviews while dealing with precision, consistency, and efficiency demands.

More than half of HR departments are understaffed, with 57% of professionals working beyond capacity. The right employee management software isn’t nice to have, it’s essential for simplifying workflows, cutting manual tasks, and giving overextended teams some much-needed breathing room.

We reviewed the 8 best employee management software to help you find the right fit for your team.

Why Listen to Us?

At Checkwriters, we’ve built a customer-centric HR and payroll platform for HR professionals. 

From applicant tracking and onboarding to payroll and compliance, our tools help simplify your day-to-day work. Our clients report increased efficiency and satisfaction, highlighting our commitment to helping you manage the entire employee lifecycle with ease. 

What is Employee Management Software (and Why Should You Care)?

Employee management software automates the core HR tasks that eat up your day: hiring, onboarding, payroll, time tracking, and benefits administration. Instead of juggling spreadsheets and manual processes, you get a centralized system that handles everything from posting jobs to processing performance reviews.

The real value goes beyond automation:

Eliminates errors in payroll and employee records through centralized data

Keeps you compliant with real-time updates on labor law changes

Delivers actionable insights through real-time reporting and analytics

Improves employee experience with smooth onboarding and transparent processes

Frees up strategic time by automating administrative busy work

For example, Checkwriters lets HR professionals manage performance reviews from one place while getting updates on global labor laws.

With more than half of HR departments understaffed, the right software transforms overwhelmed teams into strategic powerhouses focused on building great employee experiences and driving business results.

8 Best Employee Management Software for HR Success

Software Starting Price Key Strengths Best For Free Trial/Plan Payroll Integration
Checkwriters Custom pricing All-in-one platform, dedicated support, biometric time tracking Organizations wanting complete HR & payroll integration Demo available ✅ Built-in

1. Checkwriters

Checkwriters is a comprehensive, all-in-one payroll and HR platform built for organizations of all sizes. HR professionals leverage it to streamline the entire employee lifecycle from recruitment to retirement by integrating applicant tracking, onboarding, time tracking, payroll, and HR management. This way, you have all you need to reduce manual work and improve accuracy without unnecessary complexity.

We emphasize a customer-centric approach, offering dedicated support and training to ensure you have all the tools you need for an effective HR strategy. It is the right tool if you want to save resources and be more organized and efficient.

Key Features

Applicant Tracking & Background Screening: Simplifies recruitment by managing job applications and conducting background checks.

Onboarding: Offers a digital onboarding system for new hires, including document handling and training.

Payroll Automation: Simplifies wage calculations, customizable pay types, direct deposit, and general ledger entry to save time and reduce payroll errors.

Attendance Tracking: Tracks worked hours, overtime, and leave through mobile clock-ins, biometric terminals, or web punch tools, all connected to payroll.

Performance Management: Offers tools for evaluations, goal-setting, and feedback cycles, with templates that can be tailored to each department or role. 

Scheduling Tools: Prevents scheduling conflicts and helps control labor costs through reusable templates and real-time alerts.

Compliance Tools: Notifies employers of changes to laws and regulations, empowering informed decision-making without providing legal advice.

Customizable Reporting: Generates reports and analyzes HR data to support strategic planning.

Pricing

Checkwriters offers custom pricing based on your organization’s size and needs. Schedule a meeting to get a demo and a custom quote.  

Pros

Fast, intuitive, and accurate payroll process.

An extensive library of instructional videos for every feature.

Personalized support for a great user experience.

Fast job posting across multiple job boards with the click of a button.

Supports biometric, desktop, and timesheet clock-ins.

Scales easily with growing teams.

Manage benefits and employee updates in one place.

Cons

Initial setup can take time, but personalized support ensures a smooth start

2. ADP Workforce Now

ADP Workforce Now is an enterprise-grade HR platform built for global payroll processing and compliance. The cloud-based system handles human resource management, time & labor tracking, and workforce analytics without the complexity of managing multiple vendors.

Check out our list of the best ADP alternatives if you’re considering a switch from ADP.

Key Features

Payroll Processing: Automates payroll with real-time processing and error detection alerts.

Benefits Administration: Streamlines enrollment and provides intuitive employee access via mobile or desktop.

Time & Attendance: Integrates time tracking with payroll, offering real-time insights to manage labor costs.

Talent Management: Supports recruitment, onboarding, performance management, and succession planning.

Pricing

ADP Workforce Now offers tiered packages. However, the prices of these packages are based on your organization’s requirements. Kindly contact ADP directly for a personalized quote.

Pros

Integrates multiple HR functions into one platform.

Reliable and accurate payroll processing.

Customizable reports for better insights.

Cons

Complex implementation for services not related to payroll

Reporting can be complicated and cumbersome.

3. Zoho People

Zoho People is a cloud-based HR software solution from Zoho Corporation. It centralizes onboarding, time tracking, attendance, performance management, and engagement tools into a single place to help businesses manage their HR processes. It also seamlessly integrates with other Zoho apps and third-party services to help you manage your workforce and ensure consistency. 

Key Features

Employee Database: Organizes and grants secure access to personal and employment data.

Performance Appraisals: Sets goals, captures continuous feedback, and runs 360° reviews.

Shift Scheduling: Assigns, rotates, and reminds users about shifts.

HR Help Desk: Handles internal support cases and tracks resolution SLAs.

Pricing

Free: Up to 5 users with basic leave and onboarding tools.

Essential HR ($1.50/user/month): Includes database, document management, and basic shift handling.

Professional ($2.50/user/month): Includes attendance, timesheets, and shift schedules.

Premium ($3.50/user/month): Includes performance, compliance analytics.

Enterprise ($5/user/month): Includes help desk, LMS, sandbox.

People Plus: Combines HRMS, payroll, engagement, and helpdesk.

Pros

Supports 360° feedback and KPI tracking

Secures data with encryption, MFA, and activity logs

Offers customizable workflows to automate HR processes

Cons

Facial login errors frustrate users

Paid plan users report slow support 

4. Deel

Deel is a global HR and payroll platform for managing international employees and contractors. It automates onboarding, compliance, and payments across 150+ countries, helping HR teams reduce manual tasks while staying ahead of regulatory challenges. It’s ideal for distributed or remote-first organizations.

Key Features

Global Payroll: Pays employees and contractors in 150+ countries, with localized tax and benefits compliance.

Automated Compliance: Generates region-specific contracts and tracks legal changes with built-in alerts.

Onboarding: Supports self-service onboarding for employees and contractors, including e-signatures and ID verification.

Benefits Management: Offers localized health, retirement, and perks packages for global teams.

Pricing

Deel offers separate pricing for payroll services and HR tools:

Payroll & Employment Services:

Global Payroll: $29/employee/month

Contractor Management: $49/contractor/month

EOR (Employer of Record): $599/employee/month

Contractor of Record: Starting at $325/contractor/month

PEO (HR + Payroll support): $95/employee/month

US Payroll: Custom pricing

HR Tools (Add-ons):

Deel Engage (performance, surveys, career tracking): $20/worker/month

Deel Compensation (global pay structures): $15/employee/month

Deel Workforce Planning (organizational change modeling): $18/employee/month

Pros

Payment processing arrives earlier than expected.

Handles compliance and tax documentation automatically.

Supports multiple payment methods and currencies

Automatically generates legally compliant contracts.

Cons

Very expensive, especially for small teams.

Withdrawal and conversion fees may be high.

5. Connecteam

Connecteam is a mobile-first employee management platform designed for deskless and frontline teams. 

It combines HR tools, scheduling, time tracking, communication, and task management into one easy-to-use app. Available on iOS, Android, and desktop, Connecteam is ideal for industries like construction, retail, and healthcare where mobility and real-time coordination are important. 

Key Features

Time Clock: Tracks employee hours with GPS verification and geofencing.

Job Scheduling: Creates and manages shifts with templates and auto-assignments.

Task Management: Assigns tasks with checklists and real-time updates.

Employee Communication: Facilitates team chat, announcements, and surveys.

Pricing

Small Business Plan: Free for up to 10 users.

Basic ($35/month): For up to 30 users; $0.50 per additional user.

Advanced ($59/month): For up to 30 users; $1.50 per additional user.

Expert ($119/month): For up to 30 users; $3.00 per additional user.

Enterprise: Custom pricing.

Pros

Offers a free plan ideal for small teams.

Time clock features improve real-time attendance tracking.

Supports onboarding and training with courses, certifications, and document tracking.

Cons

No built-in payroll processing; you’ll need to export time data to third-party systems like QuickBooks.

Deeper analytics and advanced custom workflows may require higher-tier plans.

6. Zimyo

Zimyo is a unified, cloud-based HRMS and payroll software that automates HR tasks and supports statutory compliance across multiple countries. It’s designed for businesses of all sizes, offering operations in 11 languages and serving over 2,000 clients in 38 countries. It aims to reduce manual tasks and enhance workforce management.

Key Features

Payroll Automation: Processes salaries with statutory compliance and direct bank integrations.

Attendance Management: Tracks employee attendance using geo-tagging and biometric integrations.

Performance Management: Supports goal setting, feedback, and appraisal workflows.

Employee Self-Service: Allows employees to access payslips, apply for leave, and update personal information.

Pricing

Zimyo offers three pricing tiers:

Basic ($4/user/month): Includes core HR functions and employee self-service options

Standard ($6/user/month): Adds advanced HR and time tracking options.

Enterprise ($8/user/month): Offers performance management, global payroll, and more integrations.

Pros

Affordable pricing, especially for small teams.

Comprehensive features make it adaptable to your organization’s needs

The implementation process is easy and doesn’t require heavy technical knowledge. 

Cons

Some features are less accessible on mobile compared to desktop.

Limited third-party integrations compared to competitors.

7. Justworks

Justworks is a full-service PEO (Professional Employer Organization) and payroll platform built for U.S. small-to-mid-sized businesses. It centralizes payroll, HR, benefits, compliance, and time tracking in one intuitive dashboard. This makes it a strong choice for HR teams in schools or nonprofits seeking streamlined operations.

Key Features

Payroll & Tax Filing: Automates W-2, 1099, federal, and state filings seamlessly.

Time Tracking: Integrates geofenced clock-ins and PTO management with payroll sync.

Benefits Administration: Manages health, dental, vision, 401(k), HSAs/FSAs, and commuter perks.

Compliance Support: Includes federal/state tax registrations, EPLI, and workers’ comp access. 

Pricing

Payroll: $50/month base fee + $8/employee/month

PEO Basic: $79/employee/month (tiers based on company size)

PEO Plus: $109/employee/month (adds enhanced benefits & perks)

EOR: $599/month/employee

Add-Ons:

Time Tracking: + $8/employee/month

International Contractor Payments: + $39/contractor/month

EOR (Global Hiring): $599/employee/month 

Payroll + Health Insurance: $8/month per benefits eligible employee

Pros

Delivers enterprise-level health and wellness perks to small teams

Employees can control time tracking, PTO requests, benefits, etc.

Centralized dashboard for managing time offs, leaves, sick days, and holidays.

24/7 customer support for a personalized experience

Cons

Lack of flexibility in customizing features.

Periodic downtimes with the app.

8. PeoplesHR

PeoplesHR is a cloud-based HRIS solution in Asia and Africa, built for small to mid-sized organizations. The platform centralizes employee lifecycle tasks like onboarding, attendance, payroll, performance, and engagement. 

It also helps HR teams handle everyday challenges like employee classification, skill gaps, AI-driven changes, and the need for greater efficiency. 

Key Features

Employee Records: Stores all personnel data in one searchable system.

Payroll Processing: Generates payslips and manages tax and deductions.

Performance Appraisals: Enables goal setting, feedback, and 360° reviews.

Self-Service Portal: Let employees access payslips, submit time off, and update info.

Pricing

PeoplesHR offers custom pricing based on your organization’s size and needs. Kindly schedule a meeting to get a custom quote.  

Pros

Real-time data capturing that provides up-to-date information at all times.

Responsive customer support for a great experience.

Self-service features allow employees to update their data. 

Cons

The interface may feel outdated to some users

Occasional mismatch in leave figures

Choose Checkwriters as the Right Fit To Manage Your Team

Choosing the right employee management software can transform how you hire, onboard, and support your teams. If you’re looking for a complete, reliable solution, Checkwriters deserves a closer look.

At Checkwriters, we offer an all-in-one platform built to simplify HR and payroll operations. From applicant tracking to performance management, leave management, and benefits, we empower you with all the tools you need to manage the entire employee lifecycle efficiently and seamlessly. 

Contact us today and see what better HR management looks like. Disclaimer: The information contained herein is not intended to be construed as legal advice, nor should it be relied on as such. Employers should closely monitor the rules and regulations specific to their jurisdiction(s) and should seek advice from counsel relative to their rights and responsibilities.
